title: The edge-redundant rigidity conjecture for complete graphs in $\ell_\infty^d$
source: James Cruickshank, Sean Dewar and Derek Kitson, “Algebraic connectivity in normed spaces”, arXiv:2508.00134 (2025). (https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.00134), Conjecture 5.4
statement:
Let $d\geq 2$, let $n\geq 2d+2$, and let $K_n$ denote the complete graph on $n$ vertices. A graph is **edge-redundantly rigid** in a normed space if it has a framework that is infinitesimally rigid and remains infinitesimally rigid after deleting any edge. **Edge-redundant rigidity conjecture.** For every $d\geq 2$ and every $n\geq 2d+2$, the complete graph $K_n$ is edge-redundantly rigid in $\ell_\infty^d$.

The preceding proposition rules out $K_{2d+1}$, so the conjecture asserts that the stated threshold is sufficient as well as necessary. The supplied excerpt gives no evidence that the conjecture has been resolved.
summary: The complete graph K_8 is not edge-redundantly rigid in three-dimensional l-infinity space: no well-positioned placement of K_8 remains infinitesimally rigid after the removal of every single edge. This refutes the conjecture of Cruickshank, Dewar and Kitson that K_n is edge-redundantly rigid in l-infinity^d for all n >= 2d+2, at its first open case d = 3, n = 8. The proof reduces the property to a condition on the three colour classes of the framework (every colour class meets every cut twice), derives seven forbidden four-point patterns from the geometry, and shows the resulting propositional instance unsatisfiable; the certificate (12,876 steps) is checked inside the Lean kernel by a verified checker. K_9 is edge-redundantly rigid in l-infinity^3 (proved in Lean), and so is K_n for every n >= 10 (proved in the paper only).
paste_summary: Refuted. The complete graph K_8 is not edge-redundantly rigid in three-dimensional l-infinity space, so the conjecture of Cruickshank, Dewar and Kitson that K_n is edge-redundantly rigid in l-infinity^d for all n >= 2d+2 fails at its first open case d = 3, n = 8. The proof is computer-assisted: a reduction to colour classes of the framework, seven forbidden four-point patterns, and an unsatisfiable propositional instance whose certificate is checked inside the Lean kernel. K_9 is edge-redundantly rigid in the same space.
caveat: Computer-assisted: the unsatisfiability certificate is checked by a checker proved sound in Lean and evaluated in the kernel; the generated certificate modules are reproducible from the scripts and inputs in this folder. The journal version of the source (Linear Algebra Appl. 739, 2026) is unread. The extension of the positive result to n >= 10 is proved on paper only.
